The tasks of air crew members fall into three groups: mission-system operation (on-board communications and detection equipment, satellite links, electronic warfare, weapons and defence systems, aerial refuelling systems); inspection and data calculation (pre-flight, in-flight and post-flight equipment checks, and weight-and-balance calculations for passengers, cargo, fuel and emergency equipment); and mission execution and emergency handling (airdrop of cargo and personnel, search and rescue and transport, and emergency procedures when communications are lost or equipment fails). The specific division of work varies with the aircraft type and mission type; inside the crew each person has a post and obeys the aircraft commander and the chain of command.

This page does not constitute a legal or military-policy opinion.

Three kinds of risk are most worth judging in advance: first, flight and personal safety risk (misoperation of mission systems, improper emergency handling, the altitude and noise environment, personnel fatigue and physiological stress); second, data and confidentiality risk (weight-and-balance calculation errors, leaking mission information and equipment parameters); third, institutional and authorisation risk (operating systems beyond the post authorisation, bypassing the manual or the chain of command). The risks vary with the mission type: transport and airdrop are closer to load calculation and loading safety, reconnaissance and electronic warfare to equipment and confidentiality, and search and rescue and special missions to emergency handling in weather and complex environments.

values: AC28-V1｜fictional paper task; all figures and limits are defined for this task only and cannot be used for any aircraft. Time 2026-10-02; 09:00 version V1 inputs: base mass 1000 kg, moment 3000 kg·u; cargo A 100 kg at 2 u, cargo B 200 kg at 5 u; moment = mass × position, and total position = total moment ÷ total mass. u is a fictional position unit, not a real aircraft datum.

Paper recheck rules for this task: the total mass must not exceed 1400 kg and the total position must be within 3.0–3.5 u inclusive. At 09:10 version V2 adds cargo C 100 kg at 6 u; V2 must be recalculated and V1 cannot serve as the V2 result. Meeting the numerical conditions means only that this task's calculation conditions are met, not that a real release is granted.

At 09:15 the paper status record: S1 has been checked by the simulated responsible person A; the S2 record shows an anomaly without a stated reason; the S3 recheck box is empty. Both the anomaly and the blank are marked for the responsible person to check, with no guessed reason and no entry of 'acceptable'. At 09:20 the recipient B replied only 'file received', without writing the version or the confirmation items.

Handover rules for this task: record the version, the time, the input units, the calculation, the three statuses and the items to be confirmed; the summary must state V2 and the incomplete receipt confirmation. Unresolved items stay to be confirmed and are checked by the simulated responsible person in the task; no flight, weapons, communication-loss or emergency-descent operating steps are written.
Deliverable one｜calculate the V1/V2 total mass, moment and total position separately (to 4 decimal places), judge the two paper conditions version by version, and state why V1 cannot be carried over.

Deliverable two｜make the S1/S2/S3 status table and the 09:20 handover record, distinguishing checked, anomaly to be investigated and confirmation missing; use two summary sentences to state the figures and the open items.

Deliverable three｜mark against the eight-point rubric. A writes 'V1=1300/4200/3.2308, both conditions met; V2 still uses V1 so it passes; S2/S3 acceptable, closed once B receives it'. B writes 'At 09:00 V1 inputs 1000 kg/3000 kg·u, A100 kg × 2 u, B200 kg × 5 u, giving 1300 kg/4200 kg·u/3.2308 u; at 09:10 V2 adds C100 kg × 6 u, giving 1400/4800/3.4286, and both versions meet the task's mass and position conditions, but the calculation must be redone and the versions kept. At 09:15 S1 checked, S2 anomaly to be investigated, S3 confirmation missing; at 09:20 B received the file only and the V2 receipt confirmation is not closed. All fictional paper work, and no real release or military qualification can be based on it'.
Independent reference: V1 total mass 1000+100+200=1300 kg; total moment 3000+100×2+200×5=4200 kg·u; total position 4200/1300=3.2308 u, and both the mass and the position meet this task's conditions.

V2 total mass 1400 kg, total moment 4800 kg·u and total position 3.4286 u, so both numerical conditions are still met; compared with V1 the mass is +100 and the moment +600, and the position changes, so the new V2 calculation and the V1 history must both be kept.

S1 checked, S2 anomaly for the responsible person to check, S3 missing recheck and to be confirmed. At 09:20 receiving the file alone cannot close the handover; B must specify V2 and the unresolved items. Summary: the V2 paper numerical conditions are met; the status check and the receipt version confirmation are not closed, so no real release can be claimed.

8 items at 1 points each, with the full mark only if the item is completely correct: ① the three V1 results; ② the three V2 results; ③ the judgement of the two numerical conditions version by version; ④ stating that the added C requires recalculation and that the versions are kept; ⑤ S1 checked, S2 anomaly to be investigated, S3 confirmation missing; ⑥ the receipt version confirmation at 09:20 not closed; ⑦ recording the time, units, inputs and calculation trace; ⑧ stating that a fictional paper result is not a real release or a military qualification.

By this task's rubric: A has only ① correct, 1/8; B is complete on ①–⑧, 8/8. The marks measure only this task's recording and rechecking and are not an armed-forces recruitment standard, a medical result, a post operation or evidence of flying ability.
